svg.aria-label: From the visitor's browser to the pipeline: the page is served by Vercel; a question goes through Cloudflare and a tunnel to the API on the college PC, passes the CORS check and the access code, runs through the ten pipeline stages with the language models, indexes and the condition profile store on the same PC, and the answer streams back live.
svg.title: Condition-Grounded Scientific RAG - from the client to the pipeline (as built, public demo)
svg.text: Condition-Grounded Scientific RAG: from the visitor's browser to the pipeline (as built, public demo)
1 · CLIENT · THE VISITOR'S BROWSER (ANY DEVICE, NO GPU NEEDED)
The page keeps the tunnel address, then
removes it from the address bar
The code stays in this tab only
Question box and the chat history
Body: the question + the chat history
Serves the built page: HTML, JavaScript, CSS
No server code and no data; it never sees a question
Deployed from the frontend folder: npx vercel --prod
A public https address, a new one at every tunnel start
Ends the https connection and hands the request to the tunnel
The visitor never sees this PC's own address
Opened from this PC out to Cloudflare:
Only the Vercel address may read
A refusal still carries CORS headers
If not: search again, then warn
or when it is not about results
Pipeline.run(question, history) runs the ten stages in this order. After each stage a step event goes back to the page.
Two loops: stage 6 searches once more for a missing condition (back to 4); stage 9 regenerates once for an unsupported sentence (back to 8).
A skipped step costs no time. The page shows it as skipped, with the reason.
5 · THIS PC · WHAT THE STAGES USE (ALL LOCAL, NO EXTERNAL API)
No upload on the public demo
(3) the answer streams back the same way, live: step · note · result (server-sent events)
